content: Purchases above PKR 100,000 must follow formal procurement unless an approved exception applies.
Purchases above PKR 500,000 require at least three vendor quotations unless a documented and approved single-source justification applies.
A technical evaluation is required for specialized equipment, engineering services, and technically complex purchases.
The comparative statement must show vendor, price, technical compliance, delivery, warranty, and relevant commercial conditions.
A purchase order must not be issued before the required approval has been obtained.
A capital expenditure request must identify the amount, department, business justification, budget information, and required approval authority.
The requested amount must be consistent across the Purchase Request, vendor quotations, comparative statement, and approval request.
Material discrepancies between financial amounts in supporting documents require clarification before approval.
Requests exceeding the applicable delegated authority must be escalated to the appropriate approval authority.
Department Manager may approve capital expenditure requests up to PKR 500,000.
Department Director may approve capital expenditure requests up to PKR 2,000,000.
General Manager may approve capital expenditure requests up to PKR 5,000,000.
Capital expenditure requests above PKR 5,000,000 require approval by the Executive Committee.
One procurement requirement must not be split into smaller requests to avoid an approval threshold.
A Purchase Request must be prepared for the procurement requirement.
A Business Justification must document the business need.
Required vendor quotations must be obtained according to procurement thresholds.
Technical evaluation is required where the purchase involves specialized equipment.
A Comparative Statement must be prepared for competitive procurement.
The procurement must undergo financial review before approval.
Required approval must be obtained before purchase order issuance.
Purchase Order may be issued only after required approval.

For competitive procurement above PKR 500,000, mandatory documentation includes Purchase Request, Business Justification, Three Quotations, Technical Evaluation, Comparative Statement, and Required Approval.
Technical compliance must be evaluated for specialized purchases.
Commercial evaluation should consider price, payment terms, delivery, and warranty.
Lowest price alone does not automatically establish technical suitability.
Selection of a non-lowest vendor requires documented justification.
Relevant previous vendor performance may be considered during evaluation.
Employees participating in procurement must disclose potential conflicts of interest.
Examples include financial interests, family relationships, personal business relationships, and other relevant relationships.
A disclosed conflict must be reviewed before the employee continues participating in the procurement.
Disclosure of a potential conflict does not automatically mean that misconduct has occurred. The matter must be reviewed by the appropriate authority.
